channel.title: Nicotine Science and Policy
channel.description: Daily digest of views, debates and discussions on nicotine science, policy, regulation and advocacy.

item.title: Vaping doubles smokers’ chances of quitting, major new report finds
item.description: A major new report finding that vaping can double smokers’ chances of quitting should bring more seriousness to the harm reduction debate. Adult smokers need tools that work in real life, not just idealised messages about abstinence. Vaping is not risk-free, but its public health value lies in helping people move away from combustible tobacco. Clear advice should reflect the evidence: quitting cigarettes is the priority, and lower-risk alternatives can help make that possible. (Published on August 28, 2026bysmokefreesweden.org)

item.title: New Zealand Drives Quit Success
item.description: New Zealand’s quit success shows what happens when smokers are given practical routes away from cigarettes. Vaping has played a visible role in accelerating the shift from combustion, especially for adults who need more than willpower or repeated warnings. The lesson is not that every policy can be copied wholesale, but that access, affordability and honest risk communication matter. Smoking falls faster when lower-risk alternatives are treated as tools, not threats. (Published on August 28, 2026byplanetofthevapes.co.uk)

item.title: When Evidence Challenges the Status Quo: Senator Dorinda Cox and Australia’s Tobacco Policy Reckoning
item.description: Evidence can be uncomfortable because it forces policy to confront its own assumptions. In tobacco control, that matters most where safer nicotine products are still treated as distractions rather than tools that may help smokers leave cigarettes behind. A serious public health debate should be able to change direction when the data changes. Protecting the status quo is not the same as protecting people from harm. (Published on August 28, 2026bysubstack.com)

item.title: JAMA Article on E-Cigarettes Makes Refreshingly Sound Recommendations to Clinicians
item.description: A JAMA article supporting clinician conversations about e-cigarettes should make the debate more precise. The evidence is strongest for adult smokers who use vaping as a route away from cigarettes, not for vague claims about nicotine use in general. That distinction matters because policy can either support full switching or bury it under uncertainty. Medical guidance should separate evidence from values clearly enough for smokers to understand their options. (Published on August 28, 2026bysubstack.com)
